title: Acute Chest Pain Evaluation
description: Evidence-based triage rules for acute chest discomfort, angina, and life-threatening thoracic emergencies.

risk_rules.name: Acute Coronary Syndrome / Myocardial Infarction Pattern
risk_rules.reason: The patient reported acute chest discomfort accompanied by radiation to the arm/jaw/neck and autonomic symptoms (sweating or shortness of breath). This symptom cluster is consistent with an acute cardiac event.
risk_rules.possible_concern: Acute cardiac-related condition (e.g. Acute Coronary Syndrome)

risk_rules.name: Acute Aortic Dissection Pattern
risk_rules.reason: The patient reported sudden-onset tearing or ripping chest pain radiating through to the back, which is a classic high-alert clinical red flag.

risk_rules.name: Acute Pleuritic Chest Pain with Dyspnea (Suspected PE)
risk_rules.reason: Reported chest pain exacerbated by breathing combined with shortness of breath requires urgent exclusion of pulmonary embolism or acute pneumothorax.
risk_rules.possible_concern: Pulmonary embolism or acute pleuro-pulmonary condition

risk_rules.name: Uncharacterized Chest Discomfort without Emergency Flags
risk_rules.reason: Patient reports chest discomfort without overt autonomic or radiation red flags; clinical review is indicated to establish etiology.
risk_rules.possible_concern: Undifferentiated chest discomfort (cardiac, esophageal, or musculoskeletal)

risk_rules.name: Reproducible Musculoskeletal Chest Wall Pain
risk_rules.reason: Pain is specifically reproducible by palpation or movement without cardiac risk factors, shortness of breath, or radiation.

possible_conditions.name: Acute cardiac-related condition
possible_conditions.reason_template: Reported chest pressure/discomfort with shortness of breath, sweating, or radiation to upper extremities.
possible_conditions.caveat: These symptoms can occur with serious heart-related conditions and require urgent medical evaluation. This is decision support, not a definitive diagnosis.

possible_conditions.name: Pulmonary embolism / Pleuritic disease
possible_conditions.reason_template: Sharp or worsening pain with deep inhalation and breathlessness.
possible_conditions.caveat: Requires clinical examination, oxygen saturation assessment, and imaging if clinically indicated.

possible_conditions.name: Gastroesophageal reflux / Esophageal spasm
possible_conditions.reason_template: Burning or substernal discomfort occurring post-prandially or with recumbency.
possible_conditions.caveat: Cardiac causes must always be ruled out first before attributing symptoms to acid reflux.

possible_conditions.name: Chest wall musculoskeletal strain
possible_conditions.reason_template: Localized tenderness aggravated by positional changes, palpation, or twisting.
possible_conditions.caveat: Diagnosis of exclusion; routine clinical follow-up is advised if symptoms persist.

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Differentiates sudden vascular catastrophes from gradual or chronic onset.
recommended_questions.question: When did the chest discomfort start, and did it develop suddenly or build up gradually?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Critical safety check for hemodynamic and respiratory compromise.
recommended_questions.question: Are you having difficulty breathing or feeling short of breath?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Key hallmark of cardiac ischemia radiating to left arm, neck, shoulder, or jaw.
recommended_questions.question: Does the discomfort spread or radiate to your arm, shoulder, neck, jaw, or back?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Autonomic symptoms indicate severe systemic/cardiac stress.
recommended_questions.question: Are you experiencing profuse sweating, dizziness, lightheadedness, or nausea?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Distinguishes pressure/heaviness from sharp pleuritic or tearing pain.
recommended_questions.question: How would you describe the feeling (for example: pressure, squeezing, heaviness, sharp, or tearing)?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Monitors subjective intensity on a standard 1-10 pain scale.
recommended_questions.question: On a scale from 1 to 10 (with 10 being the most severe), how intense is the discomfort?
